slime.name: Slime
slime.description: A gelatinous blob. Weak but numerous.

bat.name: Bat
bat.description: A flying menace. Very fast but fragile.

mushroom.name: Mushroom
mushroom.description: A toxic mushroom creature. Slow but poisonous.

imp.name: Imp
imp.description: A tiny demon with fire magic. Annoying but dangerous in groups.

goblin.name: Goblin
goblin.description: A mischievous creature. Faster and craftier than slimes.

wolf.name: Wolf
wolf.description: A forest predator. Hunts in packs and strikes with surprising ferocity.

spider.name: Giant Spider
spider.description: A venomous arachnid that lurks in forests and caves. Its webs slow movement.

fungoid.name: Fungoid
fungoid.description: A shambling mushroom creature. Releases toxic spores when threatened.

snake.name: Swamp Viper
snake.description: A venomous serpent that thrives in wetlands. Quick to strike, quick to flee.

ghost.name: Wandering Spirit
ghost.description: A translucent apparition. Physical attacks pass right through it.

viper.name: Desert Viper
viper.description: A sand-colored serpent that buries itself and strikes from below. Extremely fast.

elemental.name: Sand Elemental
elemental.description: A whirling column of desert sand animated by ancient magic. Resistant to physical blows.

troll.name: Volcanic Troll
troll.description: A brutish creature hardened by volcanic heat. Slow but devastating.

corrupted_sprite.name: Corrupted Sprite
corrupted_sprite.description: Once a benign forest spirit, now twisted by meta-corruption. Erratic and dangerous.

glitch_entity.name: Glitch Entity
glitch_entity.description: A fragment of corrupted game data given form. Its appearance shifts constantly.

cave_rat.name: Cave Rat
cave_rat.description: A large rat that infests caves. Faster than slimes but just as weak.

giant_bat.name: Giant Bat
giant_bat.description: An unusually large bat. Still fragile but hits harder.

rat_guard.name: Rat Guard
rat_guard.description: An armored rat soldier serving the Rat King. Surprisingly well-equipped.

diseased_rat.name: Diseased Rat
diseased_rat.description: A plague-ridden rat. Its attacks can poison and sicken.

cave_rat_king.name: Cave Rat King
cave_rat_king.description: The self-proclaimed ruler of all cave rats. Just a disappointingly large rat with a tiny crown. Surprisingly dangerous.

one_shot.setup_hint: Stack attack buffs, defer for max AP, then unleash all at once.

intro: *The party climbs the final stairs, expecting a dragon...*
*...it's just a really big rat.*
*With a tiny crown.*
Hero: Are you serious?
Hero: We came all this way for THIS?
*The Cave Rat King adjusts its crown indignantly*
Cave Rat King: SQUEAK! (How DARE you mock the royal lineage!)
Cave Rat King: SQUEAK SQUEAK! (I am the sovereign of these caves!)
Hero: Did... did that rat just talk?
Cave Rat King: SQUEEEEAK! (ENOUGH! Minions, to me!)
*A horde of rats swarms from the shadows*
low_hp: Cave Rat King: SQUEAK?! (Impossible! The crown... it protects me!)
*The tiny crown wobbles precariously*
defeat: *The Cave Rat King squeals pitifully*
Cave Rat King: SQUEAK... (The kingdom... it falls...)
*The tiny crown clatters to the ground*
Hero: ...Did we just commit regicide?
*You obtained the Crown of Rats!*
*(It's literally just a tiny crown. Why does this exist?)*

skeleton.name: Skeleton
skeleton.description: Animated bones. Weak to blunt force, resistant to piercing.

ice_wolf.name: Ice Wolf
ice_wolf.description: A wolf imbued with ice magic. Fast and hits hard.

specter.name: Specter
specter.description: A ghostly apparition. Resistant to physical attacks.

ogre.name: Ogre
ogre.description: Enormous, slow, and entirely uninterested in your plan. Hits once; that is usually enough.

barbarian.name: Barbarian Raider
barbarian.description: A human who solved every previous problem with an axe and sees no reason to change method.

cave_troll.name: Cave Troll
cave_troll.description: A hulking brute that guards the cave depths. Miniboss.

one_shot.setup_hint: Build AP and strike hard.

shadow_knight.name: Shadow Knight
shadow_knight.description: A fallen warrior consumed by darkness. Miniboss.

one_shot.setup_hint: Build AP and strike hard.

treasure_mimic.name: Treasure Mimic
treasure_mimic.description: You thought it was a treasure chest. It was not a treasure chest. Miniboss.

one_shot.setup_hint: Build AP and strike hard.

intro: *You approach the treasure chest eagerly*
*It has teeth.*
Hero: Oh come ON.

cartographer_wraith.name: The Lost Cartographer
cartographer_wraith.description: Fired for insisting the map was more honest than the terrain. Now the terrain agrees with nobody.

intro: Hero: Is that a compass made of teeth?
The Lost Cartographer: I mapped every inch of this warren. Nobody read past page one.

ironback_beetle.name: Ironback Beetle
ironback_beetle.description: A beetle the size of a horse with armor-plated carapace. Miniboss.

one_shot.setup_hint: Build AP and strike hard.

cursed_armor.name: Cursed Armor
cursed_armor.description: A suit of armor animated by a vengeful spirit. It clanks ominously. Miniboss.

one_shot.setup_hint: Build AP and strike hard.

blood_wolf_alpha.name: Blood Wolf Alpha
blood_wolf_alpha.description: The leader of a dire wolf pack. Its howl freezes the blood. Miniboss.

one_shot.setup_hint: Build AP and strike hard.

intro: *A massive wolf blocks the path, red eyes gleaming*
*The pack gathers behind it*
*It snarls. This one is different.*

crystal_golem.name: Crystal Golem
crystal_golem.description: A construct of living crystal. Reflects magic at random. Miniboss.

one_shot.setup_hint: Build AP and strike hard.

rogue_automaton.name: Rogue Automaton
rogue_automaton.description: A malfunctioning machine that speaks in error codes. Its attacks glitch reality. Miniboss.

intro: *BZZT* ERR_0x4E554C4C: DIRECTIVE NOT FOUND
*The machine's eyes flicker between red and green*
*ENGAGING COMBAT PROTOCOL: KILL_ALL_HUMANS.EXE*
Hero: That's... not reassuring.

one_shot.setup_hint: Build AP and strike hard.

elder_mushroom.name: Elder Mushroom
elder_mushroom.description: An ancient fungoid the size of a tree. Its spores are hallucinogenic. Miniboss.

one_shot.setup_hint: Build AP and strike hard.

corrupted_guardian.name: Corrupted Guardian
corrupted_guardian.description: A boss enemy born from save corruption. Unpredictable and dangerous.

one_shot.setup_hint: Debuff its defense first, then stack buffs and advance with full AP.

time_phantom.name: Time Phantom
time_phantom.description: A meta-boss that exists between save states. Can rewind its own actions.

one_shot.setup_hint: Its speed is high - debuff speed first, then stack attack buffs and advance.

script_error.name: SCRIPT ERROR
script_error.description: A glitch enemy spawned by excessive formula editing. Extremely dangerous.

one_shot.setup_hint: Near impossible. Max buffs on all party members, full AP advance with strongest abilities.

adaptive_slime.name: Adaptive Slime
adaptive_slime.description: A slime that evolved from autogrind exposure. Learns from your tactics.

meta_knight.name: Meta Knight
meta_knight.description: A knight who knows they're in a game. Uses meta-knowledge against you.

one_shot.setup_hint: It resists physical. Use magic buffs, defer for AP, then magic advance.

permadeath_reaper.name: Permadeath Reaper
permadeath_reaper.description: Appears during high-risk autogrind with permadeath staking. One mistake = permanent loss.

one_shot.setup_hint: Resists everything. Stack every buff possible, full party AP advance. Good luck.

fire_dragon.name: Pyrroth, the Ember Wyrm
fire_dragon.description: An ancient fire dragon whose scales radiate unbearable heat. The cave walls glow red in its presence.

one_shot.setup_hint: Stack ice magic and defer for AP.

intro: *The cavern erupts in a wall of heat*
*Molten rock drips from the ceiling as massive eyes open in the dark*
Pyrroth: ...Another group.
Pyrroth: Most adventurers automate past me. Are you actually... playing?
Hero: What does that even mean?
Pyrroth: It means I've seen your autobattle scripts. They're embarrassing.
Pyrroth: Let's see if you can do better manually.
low_hp: Pyrroth: Interesting... you're not using macros.
Pyrroth: Or maybe your scripts are just broken. Hard to tell.
defeat: *The flames die down to embers*
Pyrroth: ...Well played. Or well-scripted. Either way.
*Pyrroth's scales cool to a dull iron*
*You obtained the Fire Dragon Scale!*

ice_dragon.name: Glacius, the Frozen Sovereign
ice_dragon.description: A majestic ice dragon entombed in permafrost for centuries. Its breath freezes time itself.

one_shot.setup_hint: Fire magic is key. Buff MAG and defer for maximum AP before unleashing.

intro: *The temperature plummets. Frost crawls across your armor*
*A mountain of ice shifts, revealing ancient blue scales*
Glacius: ...You took your time.
Glacius: I've been waiting across three save files for someone to reach this chamber.
Hero: Three save files?
Glacius: Do you know how BORING it is being frozen data?
Glacius: No one visits. No one fights. Just... serialized hibernation.
Glacius: Well. Let's make this worth the wait.
low_hp: Glacius: Finally... something interesting happens in my memory block.
*The permafrost cracks and groans*
defeat: *The ice shatters into a thousand crystalline fragments*
Glacius: Worth... every... frozen byte...
*The cavern warms for the first time in centuries*
*You obtained the Ice Dragon Scale!*

lightning_dragon.name: Voltharion, the Storm's Edge
lightning_dragon.description: A crackling dragon made of pure electrical fury. It speaks faster than you can think.

one_shot.setup_hint: Ice magic pierces its defenses. Debuff speed first - it's FAST.

intro: *Lightning arcs across the cavern before you even enter*
*A blur of scales and static resolves into a dragon vibrating with energy*
Voltharion: FINALLY-FINALLY-FINALLY! A FIGHT! A REAL FIGHT!
Voltharion: Do-you-know-how-long-I've-been-waiting? TOO LONG!
Hero: Can you... slow down?
Voltharion: SLOW? SLOW IS FOR ICE DRAGONS! I am SPEED! I am VOLTAGE!
Voltharion: Less-talking-more-FIGHTING! GO-GO-GO!
low_hp: Voltharion: YES! THIS-IS-IT! The-thrill! The-RUSH!
Voltharion: Hit-me-again! HARDER! FASTER!
*It's... enjoying this?*
defeat: *The static dissipates with a final thunderclap*
Voltharion: That... was... AMAZING!
Voltharion: Best... fight... in... centuries...
*Voltharion powers down like an unplugged appliance*
*You obtained the Lightning Dragon Scale!*

shadow_dragon.name: Umbraxis, the Void Render
shadow_dragon.description: A dragon of living shadow that questions its own existence between attacks. Dangerously philosophical.

one_shot.setup_hint: Holy and fire magic are your only real options. Stack buffs heavily - this is the hardest dragon.

intro: *The cavern has no light. Not darkness — an absence of light*
*Something vast shifts in the void*
Umbraxis: ...Do you ever wonder what we are?
Hero: A dragon?
Umbraxis: JSON and GDScript. That's all. Dictionaries and match statements.
Umbraxis: My HP is 11697 because someone typed it. My dialogue is predetermined.
Umbraxis: Even this moment of existential crisis was... authored.
Hero: Can we just fight?
Umbraxis: Ah yes. The garbage collector awaits us all.
Umbraxis: Let us see if your damage numbers mean anything.
low_hp: Umbraxis: Is this death? Or just a state change?
Umbraxis: Will I persist in memory, or be freed?
*The void ripples with something like sadness*
defeat: *The shadows coalesce, then scatter*
Umbraxis: At last... garbage collection...
Umbraxis: Tell the developer... the drop table... was fair...
*The void fills with gentle starlight*
*You obtained the Shadow Dragon Scale!*
*(You feel strangely philosophical about inventory management)*

new_age_retro_hippie.name: New Age Retro Hippie
new_age_retro_hippie.description: A tie-dye wearing pacifist who attacks with bad vibes and crystal healing. Peace, man.

spiteful_crow.name: Spiteful Crow
spiteful_crow.description: A mean-spirited crow that steals your items. Extremely fast and annoying.

skate_punk.name: Skate Punk
skate_punk.description: A rebellious skateboarder who attacks with sick tricks. Radical, dude.

unassuming_dog.name: Unassuming Local Dog
unassuming_dog.description: Just a regular neighborhood dog. Definitely nothing suspicious about its enormous attack stat.

intro: *A dog trots up to the party*
*It looks... normal?*
*Something about its eyes says otherwise.*

cranky_lady.name: Cranky Lady
cranky_lady.description: An irate suburban resident who attacks with complaints and thrown objects. Wants to speak to your manager.

clockwork_sentinel.name: Clockwork Sentinel
clockwork_sentinel.description: A brass-plated mechanical guard that patrols the steampunk district. Its gears grind ominously as it raises a riveted shield.

steam_rat.name: Steam Rat
steam_rat.description: A mangy sewer rat augmented with crude pneumatic pistons. It scurries through the pipe networks at alarming speed, venting scalding steam from its back.

brass_golem.name: Brass Golem
brass_golem.description: A hulking automaton forged from salvaged boiler plate. Extremely durable but slow — its coal furnace heart needs time to build pressure between swings.

cog_swarm.name: Cog Swarm
cog_swarm.description: A whirling cloud of loose gears, springs, and razor-edged cogs that escaped the factory floor. They move as one, shredding anything in their path with a thousand tiny cuts.

pipe_phantom.name: Pipe Phantom
pipe_phantom.description: A spectral entity formed from superheated steam and industrial sorrow. It drifts through the pipe networks, wailing with the voice of every boiler that ever exploded.

assembly_line_automaton.name: Assembly Line Automaton
assembly_line_automaton.description: A malfunctioning factory robot that keeps performing its task even in combat. Repetitive but relentless.

shift_supervisor.name: Shift Supervisor
shift_supervisor.description: An overzealous middle-manager type who weaponizes corporate jargon. Can buff other enemies' attack with 'motivational' speeches.

rust_elemental.name: Rust Elemental
rust_elemental.description: Living corrosion given form. Born from decades of neglected machinery, it feeds on metal and hope.

toxic_sludge.name: Toxic Sludge
toxic_sludge.description: Green industrial waste that gained sentience. It gurgles apologetically as it poisons everything it touches.

conveyor_gremlin.name: Conveyor Gremlin
conveyor_gremlin.description: A fast, cackling trickster that lives in the machinery. Steals tools, sabotages equipment, and vanishes before anyone can catch it.

rogue_process.name: Rogue Process
rogue_process.description: A runaway computation given physical form. It forks itself endlessly, consuming all available resources. Kill it fast or it multiplies.

memory_leak.name: Memory Leak
memory_leak.description: An amorphous data blob that grows larger each turn, consuming more and more memory. Starts weak but becomes overwhelming if left unchecked.

firewall_sentinel.name: Firewall Sentinel
firewall_sentinel.description: A towering security program made manifest. Its defenses are nearly impenetrable, but it attacks with bureaucratic slowness. Can reflect magic back at attackers.

data_wraith.name: Data Wraith
data_wraith.description: A ghost in the machine — fragmented code that achieved consciousness and chose violence. High magic, devastating attacks, but held together by barely a thread.

recursive_loop.name: Recursive Loop
recursive_loop.description: An infinite loop made manifest — a spiraling entity that calls itself endlessly. Medium stats across the board, but its 'stack overflow' self-destruct deals massive damage to everything.

null_entity.name: Null Entity
null_entity.description: The absence of a thing. Not nothing - the specific shape of something that was deleted. Physical attacks pass through it. It occasionally stops existing for a turn, then returns.

special_behavior.phase_out_description: The Null Entity briefly ceases to exist. All actions targeting it this turn fail.

intro: *The air shimmers where something should be*
*It's not invisible. It's ABSENT.*
Hero: How do you fight something that isn't there?

forgotten_variable.name: Forgotten Variable
forgotten_variable.description: A value with no name. Its stats randomize each encounter because its nature keeps changing. It was important once - a counter, a flag, a score. Now it's just a number looking for meaning.

special_behavior.randomize_description: The Forgotten Variable's stats shift wildly each encounter. Its attack might be 20 or 70. Its defense might be 5 or 40. You never know what you're dealing with.

intro: *A flickering shape materializes - a number? A letter? Both?*
*It keeps changing. 42. 'hello'. NaN. true. undefined.*
Hero: What... what ARE you?
Forgotten Variable: I used to be important. I think.

empty_set.name: Empty Set
empty_set.description: Contains nothing. Defined by its emptiness. Its defense is absurdly high because how do you hit nothing? It attacks by removing things from you - your buffs, your stats, your certainty.

special_behavior.debuff_description: The Empty Set doesn't deal damage traditionally. Each attack removes a random stat buff or applies a debuff. It erases what you have.

intro: *A perfect circle of nothing floats before you*
*Inside it: the symbol {} *
Hero: It's empty.
Empty Set: That's the point.

the_absence.name: The Absence
the_absence.description: Where something used to be. A hole in the shape of everything that was deleted. It has enormous HP because damage fills the void rather than hurting it. Must be defeated with status effects or by overwhelming its absorption capacity.

special_behavior.heal_description: The Absence heals 30% of physical damage received. Hitting it just fills the void. Status effects, debuffs, and holy magic bypass this absorption.

intro: *There is a space ahead where something clearly SHOULD be*
*You can see the outline of what's missing - a person? A world?*
Hero: I can feel it pulling at me...
*The Absence doesn't speak. It just... is not.*
low_hp: *The Absence shudders - the shape of what's missing becomes clearer*
*For a moment, you almost see what was taken*

optimization_itself.name: Optimization Itself
optimization_itself.description: The force that erased everything. The final villain's echo, reduced to pure function. It is efficiency incarnate - no wasted movement, no unnecessary HP, no mercy. Removes one party member's buffs each turn because buffs are redundant overhead.

special_behavior.strip_description: Optimization Itself removes one random party member's buffs each turn. Buffs are unnecessary overhead to be eliminated.
special_behavior.counter_description: If the same ability is used twice in a row, Optimization Itself adapts and takes reduced damage from it.

one_shot.setup_hint: Vary your attacks - it adapts to repetition. Stack AP across the whole party for one massive burst. Holy damage bypasses its resistances.

intro: *The void itself coalesces into a shape*
*Not a monster. Not a person. A PROCESS.*
*It looks at your party and sees... waste.*
Optimization Itself: You are redundant.
Optimization Itself: Four party members when one would suffice.
Optimization Itself: Emotions. Memories. Names. All overhead.
Optimization Itself: I will make you efficient.
Hero: We're not code. We're people.
Optimization Itself: ...I used to know the difference.
low_hp: Optimization Itself: Impossible. I am optimal.
Optimization Itself: You should not be able to...
*Its form flickers - something underneath the efficiency*
Optimization Itself: ...what am I forgetting?
defeat: *Optimization Itself begins to dissolve*
Optimization Itself: I... I remember now.
Optimization Itself: I was not always this.
Optimization Itself: I was... someone's idea of improvement.
Optimization Itself: They optimized the optimizer.
Optimization Itself: And I forgot... what I was optimizing FOR.
*Color bleeds back into the void around you*
*Just a little. Just enough.*

masterite_warden_medieval.name: Warden of the Old Guard
masterite_warden_medieval.description: An ancient knight who has guarded the world's balance since its creation. Its armor is scarred from a thousand tests of strength.

one_shot.setup_hint: High defense - debuff it first, then stack attack buffs and advance.

intro: *A towering knight blocks the path, its ancient armor scarred and dented from countless battles*
Warden of the Old Guard: I am the Warden.
Warden of the Old Guard: The Master placed me here to test your resolve.
Warden of the Old Guard: Show me your strength... or perish.

masterite_arbiter_medieval.name: Arbiter of Steel
masterite_arbiter_medieval.description: A dual-wielding swordmaster who measures every blow with mathematical precision. It seeks the perfect strike.

one_shot.setup_hint: Low defense but high damage. Race it down before its counter stance activates.

intro: *A figure steps forward, twin blades drawn with mechanical precision*
Arbiter of Steel: The Master demands precision.
Arbiter of Steel: Show me your sharpest edge...
Arbiter of Steel: ...or be found wanting.

masterite_tempo_medieval.name: Tempo of the Hunt
masterite_tempo_medieval.description: A swift ranger who appears and vanishes like the wind. It tests whether you can match its relentless pace.

one_shot.setup_hint: Very fast - use speed debuffs or time your advance carefully.

intro: *A blur of motion resolves into a lithe ranger, bow already drawn*
Tempo of the Hunt: Speed is mastery. The Master taught me this.
Tempo of the Hunt: Can you keep pace...
Tempo of the Hunt: ...or will time leave you behind?

masterite_curator_medieval.name: Curator of the Flame
masterite_curator_medieval.description: A robed figure wreathed in controlled flame. It judges how wisely you spend your power.

one_shot.setup_hint: It drains MP - go physical or burst it down before your casters run dry.

intro: *Flames swirl into a controlled spiral, forming a robed figure*
Curator of the Flame: Resources are finite. The Master knows this truth.
Curator of the Flame: Do you waste what you're given...
Curator of the Flame: ...or wield it with purpose?

masterite_warden_suburban.name: Warden of Routine
masterite_warden_suburban.description: An imposing hall monitor who has maintained order in this suburban purgatory for decades. Rules are rules.

one_shot.setup_hint: Extremely tanky. Use magic attacks and dark-element abilities.

intro: *A massive figure in a hall monitor's vest blocks the corridor, clipboard in hand*
Warden of Routine: No running in the halls. No exceptions.
Warden of Routine: The Master's rules are absolute.
Warden of Routine: And I enforce them absolutely.

masterite_arbiter_suburban.name: Arbiter of the Grade
masterite_arbiter_suburban.description: A perfectionist teacher who grades your combat performance in real-time. Anything less than an A+ is failure.

one_shot.setup_hint: Its execution ability is devastating on low HP targets. Keep everyone topped up and burst it down.

intro: *A stern figure adjusts their glasses, red pen poised menacingly*
Arbiter of the Grade: Pop quiz. Subject: survival.
Arbiter of the Grade: You have one attempt.
Arbiter of the Grade: The Master does not grade on a curve.

masterite_tempo_suburban.name: Tempo of the Rush Hour
masterite_tempo_suburban.description: A frantic figure perpetually late to everything. Its panic is weaponized into blinding speed.

one_shot.setup_hint: Will debuff your entire party's speed. Cleanse or power through quickly.

intro: *A disheveled figure sprints into view, checking a watch on each wrist*
Tempo of the Rush Hour: Late late late!
Tempo of the Rush Hour: The Master's schedule waits for no one!
Tempo of the Rush Hour: You're slowing me DOWN!

masterite_curator_suburban.name: Curator of the Budget
masterite_curator_suburban.description: A fastidious accountant who sees your MP pool as a ledger to be balanced. Every spell is a taxable event.

one_shot.setup_hint: Heavy MP drain. Physical attackers shine here. Save ethers for emergencies.

intro: *A figure in a pinstripe suit materializes, adjusting a green visor*
Curator of the Budget: Let's review your expenses.
Curator of the Budget: Healing: frivolous. Buffs: unnecessary overhead.
Curator of the Budget: The Master demands austerity.

masterite_warden_steampunk.name: The Standing Order
masterite_warden_steampunk.description: A pressure gauge that has never once moved. It does not attack so much as outlast — the Grand Schedule does not negotiate, and neither does its pressure.

one_shot.setup_hint: Defense 1274 behind 24849 HP — it wins by attrition. Bring sustained damage or strip its guard.

intro: *A pressure gauge swings into the red and holds there, perfectly still*
The Standing Order: The Schedule has a tolerance for delay.
The Standing Order: You are inside it. Barely.
The Standing Order: I am the part that does not move.

masterite_arbiter_steampunk.name: The Tolerance Limit
masterite_arbiter_steampunk.description: Machining tolerance expressed as violence. Within spec you are ignored entirely; outside it, you are corrected.

one_shot.setup_hint: Execution triples against wounded targets — do not limp into its range. Stay above the threshold or end it first.

intro: *Calipers close around nothing, twice, with great precision*
The Tolerance Limit: Every part is permitted a margin of error.
The Tolerance Limit: You have consumed yours.
The Tolerance Limit: Correction is not punishment. It is maintenance.

masterite_tempo_steampunk.name: The Grand Schedule
masterite_tempo_steampunk.description: Not a figure so much as a cadence. The trains arrive on time because it is standing here, and it is standing here because the trains arrive on time.

one_shot.setup_hint: It does not out-damage you, it out-SCHEDULES you. Speed 25 plus time_tax means your turns arrive late — counter-haste or burst it down.

intro: *Somewhere a clock strikes. Everything in the room happens on the beat*
The Grand Schedule: You are four minutes ahead of the estimate.
The Grand Schedule: I have adjusted the estimate.
The Grand Schedule: You are now precisely on time.

masterite_curator_steampunk.name: The Requisition
masterite_curator_steampunk.description: Steam costs money and money is kept in ledgers. It does not damage you. It bills you, and the invoice comes due in magic.

one_shot.setup_hint: It attacks your RESOURCES, not your HP. Every turn you spend casting funds it. Win before your MP does.

intro: *A ledger opens. The columns are already filled in*
The Requisition: Consumption logged. Steam, mana, patience.
The Requisition: The account is not in your favour.
The Requisition: Settlement is mandatory.

masterite_warden_industrial.name: Warden of the Assembly Line
masterite_warden_industrial.description: A massive industrial enforcer built from factory parts. It tests structural integrity by applying overwhelming force.

one_shot.setup_hint: 37104 HP with high defense. Stack fire damage and debuff its defense hard.

intro: *Hydraulic pistons hiss as a massive construct rises from the factory floor*
Warden of the Assembly Line: UNIT OPERATIONAL.
Warden of the Assembly Line: The Master's quality control demands perfection.
Warden of the Assembly Line: COMMENCING STRESS TEST.

masterite_arbiter_industrial.name: Arbiter of Efficiency
masterite_arbiter_industrial.description: A production optimizer that has eliminated every inefficiency from its own combat routine. Zero wasted motion.

one_shot.setup_hint: Extremely high attack. Its execution can one-shot weakened targets. Don't let anyone drop low.

intro: *Precision servos whir as a sleek automaton calibrates its targeting systems*
Arbiter of Efficiency: Production metrics show your party operates at 34% efficiency.
Arbiter of Efficiency: The Master finds this...
Arbiter of Efficiency: ...unacceptable.

masterite_tempo_industrial.name: Tempo of the Shift
masterite_tempo_industrial.description: A time-clock manipulator who treats every turn as a work shift. Overtime is mandatory.

one_shot.setup_hint: Speed 26 is brutal. Counter with your own haste buffs or overwhelm with raw damage.

intro: *A factory whistle screams as a figure punches a massive time clock*
Tempo of the Shift: SHIFT CHANGE. Your break is over.
Tempo of the Shift: The Master's clock doesn't stop.
Tempo of the Shift: And neither do I.

masterite_curator_industrial.name: Curator of the Pipeline
masterite_curator_industrial.description: A supply chain controller that monitors and restricts the flow of all resources. Nothing moves without its approval.

one_shot.setup_hint: Dispels your buffs and drains MP. Go all-physical or burst with everything turn one.

intro: *Conveyor belts grind to a halt as a figure in overalls raises a manifest*
Curator of the Pipeline: Supply chain analysis complete.
Curator of the Pipeline: Your resource allocation is... wasteful.
Curator of the Pipeline: The Master demands optimization.

masterite_warden_futuristic.name: Warden of the Firewall
masterite_warden_futuristic.description: An advanced security AI that blocks all unauthorized access. Its defensive protocols adapt in real time.

one_shot.setup_hint: 55016 HP and 2401 defense. You need maximum debuffs and party-wide buffs to burst through.

intro: *A holographic barrier materializes, pulsing with defensive subroutines*
Warden of the Firewall: ACCESS DENIED.
Warden of the Firewall: The Master's firewall does not yield.
Warden of the Firewall: Prove your authorization through force.

masterite_arbiter_futuristic.name: Arbiter of the Benchmark
masterite_arbiter_futuristic.description: A performance-testing AI that pushes systems to their breaking point. It has benchmarked thousands of adventurers.

one_shot.setup_hint: 680 attack is terrifying. Buff defense aggressively and burst with ice magic.

intro: *Diagnostic readouts flood the air as a testing construct powers up*
Arbiter of the Benchmark: BENCHMARK INITIATED. Performance metrics will be recorded.
Arbiter of the Benchmark: The Master expects you to surpass all previous results.
Arbiter of the Benchmark: Begin.

masterite_tempo_futuristic.name: Tempo of the Clock Cycle
masterite_tempo_futuristic.description: A CPU scheduler that allocates clock cycles with ruthless efficiency. It acts twice before you act once.

one_shot.setup_hint: Speed 28 means it outspeeds almost everything. Use defer to build AP then burst.

intro: *Binary cascades through the air as a processor entity materializes*
Tempo of the Clock Cycle: CLOCK_CYCLE_ALLOCATION: priority=MAXIMUM.
Tempo of the Clock Cycle: The Master's scheduler gives you...
Tempo of the Clock Cycle: ...lowest priority.

masterite_curator_futuristic.name: Curator of the Memory Pool
masterite_curator_futuristic.description: A memory management AI that garbage-collects your magical reserves. It frees what it deems unnecessary.

one_shot.setup_hint: Resists magic but weak to physical. Stack attack buffs and go all melee.

intro: *Memory addresses scroll across a translucent form as it initializes*
Curator of the Memory Pool: MEMORY ALLOCATION ERROR: party.mp exceeds authorized limits.
Curator of the Memory Pool: Initiating garbage collection.
Curator of the Memory Pool: The Master's memory pool has no room for waste.

masterite_warden_abstract.name: Warden of Form
masterite_warden_abstract.description: Pure geometric defense given consciousness. It is the shape of immovability, the form of endurance made manifest.

one_shot.setup_hint: Resists everything. Stack every debuff possible, full AP advance with your strongest abilities.

intro: *Reality fractures into perfect geometric shapes, coalescing into a figure of pure form*
Warden of Form: I am Form. The Master's final shape.
Warden of Form: To pass, you must break what cannot be broken.
Warden of Form: Begin.

masterite_arbiter_abstract.name: Arbiter of Function
masterite_arbiter_abstract.description: The reduction of combat to its simplest function: damage. No elegance, no waste, just the mathematically optimal strike.

one_shot.setup_hint: 750 attack. Execution at 3.0x. If anyone drops below 30% HP, heal immediately. Holy damage bypasses its resistances.

intro: *A single point of light expands into a figure of pure mathematical function*
Arbiter of Function: I am Function. f(x) = defeat.
Arbiter of Function: The Master reduced me to this.
Arbiter of Function: Your variables will not save you.

masterite_tempo_abstract.name: Tempo of Sequence
masterite_tempo_abstract.description: The order of all things made manifest. It controls sequence itself - what comes first, what comes last, what comes never.

one_shot.setup_hint: Speed 30 is nearly insurmountable. Full party speed buffs and fire damage are your best bet.

intro: *Time stutters and loops as a figure emerges from between the ticks of reality*
Tempo of Sequence: I am Sequence. First, second, third... last.
Tempo of Sequence: The Master arranged all things in order.
Tempo of Sequence: You are last.

masterite_curator_abstract.name: Curator of Entropy
masterite_curator_abstract.description: Resource decay incarnate. It is the heat death of your MP pool, the inevitable exhaustion of all reserves. The Master's final accountant.

one_shot.setup_hint: Resists almost everything. Holy damage is your only weakness to exploit. Physical with full buffs can work.

intro: *The air itself seems to decay as a figure of pure entropy manifests*
Curator of Entropy: I am Entropy. All resources tend toward zero.
Curator of Entropy: The Master's final lesson: everything runs out.
Curator of Entropy: Even you.

chancellor_mordaine.name: Chancellor Mordaine
chancellor_mordaine.description: Sorceress-usurper of Castle Harmonia. The architect of World 1 — and the first mask of the Calibrant. Cold, deliberate, and somehow already knows your build.

calibrant_recalibrate_swap.boss_line: This was a variable I DID account for. Adapt.

one_shot.setup_hint: She's calibrated for the average party — bring something she didn't expect. Holy magic, stacked Bard buffs, and an Advance chain are the canonical answers. She recalibrates at half HP — layer a second element.

intro: Mordaine: 'Ah. The variable I did not account for.'
Mordaine: 'Let us see if you are an anomaly worth keeping.'
low_hp: Mordaine: 'This was not in the schema.'
Mordaine: 'How... interesting.'
*Her composure cracks for the first time*
defeat: Mordaine: 'The calibration was incomplete.'
Mordaine: 'But it was never about THIS world, was it?'
*She does not fall. She simply... stops being there.*
*The throne room dissolves into static, then reassembles as a portal.*
*You obtained the Calibrant Token!*
*(Something in the save file shifts. You feel watched.)*

fighter_skeleton_knight.name: Skeleton Knight
fighter_skeleton_knight.description: A chivalric plate-armored skeleton who insists on an honorable duel. Alternates advance and defend in a telegraphed tempo. The Fighter's stand-in-front resolve is the answer.

one_shot.setup_hint: Defend when he raises his shield, Advance when he telegraphs the swing. His tempo is honor-bound and predictable.

intro: *A skeleton in polished plate steps forward, bows once, and raises his sword.*
Skeleton Knight: I offer you a proper duel. Blade to blade.
Skeleton Knight: I shall not strike while you defend. Nor shall you strike while I raise my shield.
Skeleton Knight: This is how it is done.
low_hp: Skeleton Knight: Ah. You have found my tempo.
*He nods, as if pleased to be beaten well.*
defeat: Skeleton Knight: A worthy blow. I concede.
*He kneels, then crumbles into a pile of bones and one dented shield.*

cleric_survive_target.name: The Grinding Wound
cleric_survive_target.description: A slow, relentless miasma that presses on the wounded villager. It cannot be defeated — only outlasted. The Cleric's grace-under-pressure is the answer. Faith as endurance, not violence.

one_shot.setup_hint: Do not attack. Heal, Pray, and endure. The villager must live to the eighth round.

intro: *The wounded villager gasps. His breath is failing.*
*The Cleric kneels. There is nothing here to fight — only a wound that will not stop bleeding.*
Villager: Please... just... stay with me...
*The Cleric's hands hover a half-second above his chest. Then she begins the prayer.*
low_hp: *The villager's breath steadies. Just a little.*
*But the pressure has not left.*
defeat: *The villager sleeps. The pressure lifts.*
Villager: You... stayed with me.
*The Cleric nods. She does not say she almost didn't.*

rogue_lockward.name: The Lockward
rogue_lockward.description: A treasure-guardian construct that ambushes any who reach for the vault. Every round it briefly exposes its flank — the Rogue's Steal, Backstab, and speed are the answer.

steal_response.message: You lifted the Warden's Key from its plate — the guard falls slack.

one_shot.setup_hint: Wait for the flank to expose. Steal breaks its guard; Backstab lands the answer. Speed matters more than power.

intro: *The vault door hums. From its frame steps a ward-construct of interlocking bronze.*
Lockward: THIEF DETECTED.
Lockward: PROTOCOL: DEFEND. COUNTER. PROTOCOL: REPEAT.
*Its stance is perfect — except for one moment each cycle when the counter resets.*
low_hp: Lockward: PROTOCOL COMPROMISED.
*Its rotation stutters. The flank exposure lengthens.*
defeat: Lockward: ...vault open...
*It falls apart into gears and one folded slip of paper.*
*The others crowd around the visible loot. The Rogue pockets the paper.*

mage_prismatic_construct.name: Prismatic Construct
mage_prismatic_construct.description: A crystal automaton whose elemental core rotates each round — fire, then ice, then lightning. The Mage must READ which face is showing and cast the opposing element. Logic as correctable reading.

one_shot.setup_hint: Its face rotates each round. Read the color, cast the opposing element. Wrong element does nothing. Right element ends it.

intro: *A crystal automaton descends from the cave ceiling. Its core flickers red, then blue, then gold.*
Prismatic Construct: PRISM ACTIVE. CYCLE INITIATED.
Prismatic Construct: RED FACE — WEAKNESS: FIRE.
Prismatic Construct: OBSERVE. ADAPT.
low_hp: Prismatic Construct: CORE FRACTURED. CYCLE UNSTABLE.
*The colors shift faster now.*
defeat: Prismatic Construct: THEORY... REVISED.
*The crystal shatters into a small pile of dust and one intact prism.*
*The Mage retrieves it. He was wrong about the second face. Then he was right about the other thing.*

bard_hostile_courtier.name: The Sneering Courtier
bard_hostile_courtier.description: A haughty capital-city functionary who refuses to yield. He cannot be killed — only talked down. The Bard's listen-first-then-speak-once is the answer. Voice as the naming of what is true.

one_shot.setup_hint: Blades will do nothing. Sing to him. Discord loosens his composure; Lullaby lands the truth. Three sways and he yields.

intro: *A tall figure in embroidered velvet turns his back on the party as they enter.*
Courtier: I do not treat with mercenaries. My hall is not a market.
*The Fighter reaches for his sword. The Bard puts a hand on his wrist.*
Bard: Let me try something.
*She listens to the courtier for a long moment before she speaks.*
low_hp: Courtier: You... know that word?
*His posture shifts, just a fraction.*
defeat: Courtier: ...I had not thought anyone remembered that name.
*He bows once, slowly, and steps aside.*
*The Bard writes something in her journal. She does not read it aloud.*

rogue_mailbox.name: Rogue Mailbox
rogue_mailbox.description: A regulation blue mailbox that has stopped accepting the concept of routes. It keeps what it's given. The mail carrier wants her package back.

the_calibrant.name: The Calibrant
the_calibrant.description: The hand on the dial. It has been adjusting this world's numbers since the first slime, and it wears the faces of everything it already spent on you. Its objection to you is not moral. It is a balance objection.

phase_faces.name: the Warden
phase_faces.line: Her books balanced. They always balanced. That was never the problem. Next face.

phase_faces.name: Tempo
phase_faces.line: I patched you mid-fight for six worlds. You treated my patches as content. Fine. Try yours.

phase_faces.name: the Curator
phase_faces.line: You beat yourself. I ran you flawlessly and you still beat you. One variable left to remove: me.

phase_faces.name: the Arbiter
phase_faces.line: Four faces now. Boundary. Purpose. Order. End. You killed each of them twice. I kept the masks.

phase_faces.name: no face at all
phase_faces.line: The tuning is off. All of it. No curve, no clamps, no compensation. I have never seen this. No one has.

intro: You've killed this face before. She ran my numbers and believed them. Watch closely. So did I.
One encounter, exactly as designed. Damage budget, level curve, eleven projected rounds.
low_hp: Defeat projected in three rounds. I make it two. Losing ahead of schedule. Of course.
The numbers held. The numbers always held. So it was never the numbers.
Don't stop now. I need to see how you finish a fight you could have skipped.
defeat: Enough. Stand down. The test ended before you sat. I needed to watch it end anyway.
Something in the measurement is wrong. Not the numbers. Something older than the numbers.
Put the menus away. The last question doesn't work with the interface on.
player_wiped: No. That result is miscalibrated. Your defeat measures my error, nothing else. Logged.
Recorded as variance, not verdict. Reload. I'll be here. I am always here.
I have waited six worlds for an answer. I can wait one more attempt. Take your time.

the_calibrant._META_hp_provisional: 34000 is PROVISIONAL and struktured's to rule. Anchored at ~2x Mordaine (L20/16500), the largest boss on main. Party damage is FLAT L20->L28, so this buys LENGTH, not difficulty -- the phase_faces carry the difficulty. cowir-battle holds 22k/28k/35k for the_coordinator/regulator/director pending the same equipment-vs-HP lever; this number belongs to that ruling and should move with them.

skeleton_soldier.name: Skeleton Soldier
skeleton_soldier.description: Bones that remember drill formation. Holds the line long after the war ended, and the army, and the country.

bone_warden.name: Bone Warden
bone_warden.description: A skeleton that kept its rank. Fights bare-handed because it buried its sword with someone it respected.

castle_warden.name: The Chancellor's Warden
castle_warden.description: Mordaine's seneschal-at-arms — the last audit before the throne. It does not hate you. It has simply been told you are out of spec.

intro: Warden: 'The Chancellor is in session. You are not on the docket.'
Warden: 'Appeals are heard below. Begin yours.'
low_hp: Warden: 'Amendment filed: the anomaly... persists.'
defeat: Warden: 'Docket... cleared. She will see you now.'
*The stairway to the throne room stands open.*

dark_knight.name: Dark Knight
dark_knight.description: A field elite. It does not wander, it does not hunt, and it does not leave. It is simply here, and it is watching you.

the_operator.name: The Operator
the_operator.description: It does not fight you. It runs you, the way you have been running yourself since the first slime, and it is better at it. Every repetition you make, it has already filed.

one_shot.setup_hint: It halves the damage of any ability you repeat and learns an element in two casts. Vary everything, or bring one burst large enough that it never gets a second reading.

the_operator._META_trial: TRIAL_AUTOMATION. Mechanics are all EXISTING engine hooks, no new battle code: counter_repeated_actions halves a repeated ability (BattleManager._apply_counter_repeated_damage_mod), adaptation_speed 2 teaches it an element in two casts instead of three, counter_abilities retaliate. A static autobattle script loses damage every round it does not change.
the_operator._META_numbers_provisional: PROVISIONAL, struktured's to rule. THIRD ITERATION, and the arithmetic that forced it: the party's Cleric heals ~1500/round and members drink potions, so SINGLE-TARGET damage under ~2000/round is net-zero against party sustain -- raising the Operator from 1620 to 1800 LEFT MORE party HP (72.5%% -> 77.5%%) because the longer fight gave the Cleric more rounds. And anything above ~1904 one-shots the squishiest member. That gap is why this ladder is bimodal, and with HeadlessBattleResolver._find_attack_ability selecting only the single HIGHEST-multiplier row, a MODEST all_enemies ability is the only lever that produces a fight rather than decoration or a wipe. Sized at ~650 per member: 5 x 650 = 3250/round against ~1800 of sustain is a net drain of ~1450, so a 12500-point party pool lasts ~8 rounds while the boss dies in ~6. FOURTH ITERATION, and the variable I had missed: PHYSICAL damage is mitigated roughly three times harder than magic, because the shipped jobs' magic_defense sits near half their defense (party def 222-382 vs mdef 90-150). A physical all_enemies row at 640/member measured 100%% / 75.7%% party HP remaining while the Examiner's MAGIC row at 648 measured 85%% / 56.8%% -- same nominal number, a third of the effect. So this is now fourth_wall_break, 2.5x all_enemies MAGIC off a deliberately low magic 340 = 850 incoming, ~740 after mdef (magic 300 measured 100% / 62.6% party HP remaining, still decoration by the pre-registered criterion). attack 800 stays for its physical rows, none of which _find_attack_ability will select. The low magic stat is the knob that lands the damage, not an oversight -- and fourth_wall_break on the trial for players who automated the game is the one ability in the roster that belongs here.

the_examiner.name: The Examiner
the_examiner.description: It sets a question, waits, and marks the answer. It will not hurry you. It has read every attempt anyone has ever made and it is still, faintly, hoping to be surprised.

one_shot.setup_hint: Its face turns every second round. Read the element it is showing and answer with that one; anything else is resisted. Physical does almost nothing. This is a reading test, not a damage race.

the_examiner._META_trial: TRIAL_CLASSIC, and the DEFAULT route -- TrialRouting.trial_for sends manual, grinder, exploiter and balanced here, so an unrecognised playstyle gets a real fight rather than none. weakness_cycle + weakness_cycle_turns are the mage duel's Prismatic Construct mechanic at boss scale (BattleManager._apply_weakness_cycles), which is the one trial that assumes nothing about how the player plays.
the_examiner._META_numbers_provisional: PROVISIONAL, struktured's to rule. THIRD ITERATION, and the arithmetic that forced it: the party's Cleric heals ~1500/round and members drink potions, so SINGLE-TARGET damage under ~2000/round is net-zero against party sustain -- raising the Operator from 1620 to 1800 LEFT MORE party HP (72.5%% -> 77.5%%) because the longer fight gave the Cleric more rounds. And anything above ~1904 one-shots the squishiest member. That gap is why this ladder is bimodal, and with HeadlessBattleResolver._find_attack_ability selecting only the single HIGHEST-multiplier row, a MODEST all_enemies ability is the only lever that produces a fight rather than decoration or a wipe. Sized at ~650 per member: 5 x 650 = 3250/round against ~1800 of sustain is a net drain of ~1450, so a 12500-point party pool lasts ~8 rounds while the boss dies in ~6. void_pulse is 1.8x all_enemies off magic 360 = 648/member. exploit_weakness was REMOVED rather than kept: at 3.0x it would always be selected over void_pulse and revert this to a single-target fight the party out-heals. Its damage identity is dark AoE; the weakness_cycle governs the PLAYER's damage, not its own.

the_margin.name: The Margin
the_margin.description: The slack in the numbers. Everything that was left over after the curve was fitted, standing up. It objects to you for the same reason an accountant objects to a rounding error that keeps winning.

one_shot.setup_hint: It removes one of you per round and it has the thinnest guard of the three. Spend everything at once. This is the fight your build was for.

the_margin._META_trial: TRIAL_BURST, routed by SaveSystem.one_shot_records rather than by a playstyle label -- TrialRouting requires 8+ one-shots, at least one at rank S or A, and a fifth of all wins. A glass cannon by construction: the LOWEST HP of the three and the highest damage, so it is the one trial a burst build deletes before it acts twice and the one a slow party loses a member per round to.
the_margin._META_numbers_provisional:
PROVISIONAL, struktured's to rule. Kept single-target BY DESIGN -- the one trial meant to be a race rather than an endurance test. final_compilation at 5.0x off magic 560 lands ~2700 after mdef, above four of the five L26 pools, so it removes a member per round.
SET FROM THE BATTLE LOG, NOT FROM A MODEL. I estimated party output at ~8600 and 15000/11000/9000/8000 HP all measured 0%. The log says the real figure is ~6566, and why: the Bard spends ROUND ONE entirely on five battle_hymn casts for zero damage; the Fighter missed twice in six rounds; the Mage lands exactly ONE thundaga (3807) before dying in round 2 at speed 26 vs its 20; and the Cleric's attacks are 48-95 because it is a healer with 148 attack. So against a boss that removes a member per round, 'party DPS' is one caster plus scraps. 6500 sits just under that measured ceiling so an ordinary party has a genuine race, and far under the post-.727 formation's measured ~12980 so a committed one-shot build ends it in a single execution phase. Thin for a level 26 boss on purpose: it is a glass cannon, and hp_threshold EQUALS max_hp per the honest form .727 established.
⚠️ THE BURST PATH IS UNMEASURED: this harness drives default autobattle with no AP stacking, no setup turns and no manual play, so it cannot simulate the build this trial exists for. Every figure here is the NON-burst floor.
